messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] AVDI - different estimates compared to "classical sampling"
parts:
Hi, in our experience ADVI has worked best when parameters are on unit scale (so, estimates not too far from 0 with uncertainties not too far from 1).  And it should be checked using multiple chains and fake data simulation.
Andrew

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] AVDI - different estimates compared to "classical sampling"
parts:
Not sure what magic you're expecting. Andrew and Alp and others are
working on figuring out why ADVI doesn't work, but I don't think they
have any concrete suggestions so far other than to keep things on a unit
scale and the more data you have so that the more multivariate normal
the unconstrained posterior is, the better.

The big problem is that we don't know how to diagnose ADVI failures
when it thinks it's converged without running MCMC, which has better
failure diagnostics.

We're always open to suggestions on how to make ADVI (or any other pieces
of Stan) better.

- Bob
